metadata.skill_name: Check Package Availability and Version Compatibility

skill_drafts.name: Check Package Availability and Version Compatibility
skill_drafts.description: Verify whether a required package is installed and meets minimum version constraints before attempting to load or instrument it. Returns a boolean indicating readiness for activation.
applicable_signals: Before instrumenting a module or loading a package-dependent feature
When deciding whether to activate an instrumentation handler
Pre-flight check before module import or feature enablement
contraindications: After a module is already loaded and active
When version constraints are not defined or unavailable
For runtime feature detection after initialization is complete
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': "Check if package_name is 'python' (stdlib special case)", 'detail': 'If true, extract sys.version_info and format as major.minor.micro'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Resolve provider_name', 'detail': "Use explicit package_name if provided; otherwise derive from module_name (last segment after split on '.')"}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Retrieve installed version', 'detail': 'Call get_library_version(provider_name) to obtain version string'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Compare versions', 'detail': 'Parse both installed version and min_version using Version class; return True if installed >= min_version'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Handle exceptions', 'detail': 'Catch all exceptions and return False without re-raising'}
triggers: Before instrumenting a module or loading a package-dependent feature; when deciding whether to activate an instrumentation handler.
constraints: Must handle stdlib modules (e.g., 'python' package_name) by checking sys.version_info
Must gracefully return False on any exception without propagating
Must use semantic versioning comparison (Version class)
cautions: Version comparison is semantic; ensure min_version is in valid format (e.g., '1.2.3')
get_library_version may return 'unknown' for uninstalled packages; treat as version mismatch
Stdlib modules require special handling; do not attempt to query version for 'python' package_name via get_library_version
output_contract: Boolean result: True if package exists and version >= min_version; False otherwise. No exceptions raised to caller.

metadata.prompt: Evaluate package availability and version compatibility by: (1) handling special cases (e.g., stdlib modules like concurrent.futures mapped to 'python'); (2) resolving the provider name from explicit package_name or derived from module_name; (3) retrieving the installed version using get_library_version; (4) comparing against min_version using semantic versioning; (5) returning False on any exception without raising.

skill_drafts.name: Resolve and Import Instrumentation Module
skill_drafts.description: Dynamically import an instrumentation module by name and return the module object for subsequent class instantiation or method access.
applicable_signals: module_name string is available and non-empty
module existence has been pre-validated or version check passed
caller needs ModuleType object for attribute access or class instantiation
contraindications: module_name is invalid, malformed, or refers to a non-existent module
version validation has not been performed before this operation
module import would raise ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Receive module_name as input', 'detail': "module_name is a string representing the dotted module path (e.g., 'concurrent.futures', 'custom.instrumentation')"}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Call importlib.import_module(module_name)', 'detail': 'Dynamically load and return the ModuleType object'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Return ModuleType object', 'detail': 'Caller can now use getattr() or direct attribute access on the module'}
triggers: When you need to obtain a module object from a stored module name string; before instantiating a class from that module.
constraints: module_name must be a valid dotted module path string
the target module must be installed and importable in the current environment
this operation does not perform version checking; assume pre-validation
cautions: importlib.import_module() will raise ImportError if the module cannot be found
side effects may occur during module import (e.g., module-level code execution)
ensure module_name is trusted and does not come from untrusted user input
output_contract: Returns a ModuleType object corresponding to module_name. The object is ready for attribute access (e.g., getattr(module, class_name) for class instantiation). If import fails, raises ImportError.

examples.notes: Standard library module import succeeds; caller can now access classes like ThreadPoolExecutor
Custom module import; caller can now instantiate classes defined in that module

metadata.prompt: Use importlib.import_module() to load the module specified by module_name. Return the ModuleType object. This operation assumes the module name is valid and the module exists in the environment.

skill_drafts.name: Instantiate Instrumentation Handler
skill_drafts.description: Create a new instance of a specified instrumentor class from a loaded module, returning a ready-to-use BaseInstrumentor object.
contraindications: Module has not been imported or is unavailable
class_name does not exist in the module
Module version does not meet minimum requirements
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Retrieve the loaded module via self.module property', 'detail': 'Uses importlib.import_module(self.module_name) internally'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Look up the class by name using getattr()', 'detail': 'getattr(self.module, self.class_name) retrieves the class object'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Instantiate the class with no arguments', 'detail': 'Calls the class constructor: getattr(self.module, self.class_name)()'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Return the BaseInstrumentor instance', 'detail': 'Instance is ready for configuration and activation by caller'}
triggers: Module is successfully loaded and imported
Need a fresh instrumentor instance for a specific package or module
constraints: Requires module to be pre-loaded via importlib.import_module()
class_name must match an actual class in the module
Instantiation assumes the class constructor takes no required arguments
cautions: If class_name is incorrect or missing, getattr will raise AttributeError
If the class constructor has required parameters, instantiation will fail
No error handling is performed; caller must catch exceptions
output_contract: Returns a BaseInstrumentor instance with no initialization errors. Instance is ready for downstream configuration and activation. If instantiation fails, an exception is raised to the caller.

metadata.prompt: Call get_instance() after confirming the module is loaded and version requirements are met. The method uses getattr to retrieve the class by name from the module, then instantiates it with no arguments. Returns a BaseInstrumentor instance ready for configuration.
